task.title: Expose declared param order in __api__ so MCP consumers dispatch positionally
acceptance_criteria: __api__(name) returns the function's positional parameter names in declaration order (e.g. param_order: [:project_name, :status]), including parameters with defaults
Order matches the generated function clause arity/positions, not map hash order
Existing hints[:params] map is unchanged (no breaking change to current consumers)
A multi-param api() function with params declared in non-alphabetical order round-trips: named args -> param_order -> positional apply hits the correct slots
moduledoc/docs note that MCP-dispatch consumers must order positional args by param_order, not Map.keys(params)
out_of_scope: Changing the MCP wire schema (input_schema properties stay a JSON object/map per spec)
Any harness-side code (consumed there in a separate, coordinated bump)
task.body:
`__api__(name)` exposes `hints[:params]` as a **map**, which discards the declaration order of the `params:` keyword list. Any consumer that maps named MCP/JSON arguments back onto a positional `apply(module, fun, args)` call has no correct source for argument order — `Map.keys/1` returns hash order, so multi-param tools get their arguments swapped.

This is the entire point of the `api()` → MCP-tool pipeline (Phase 7, tasks 19/20), so the gap breaks real dispatch. Concrete downstream failure: harness's `Harness.Chat.Tools.build_apply_args/2` (in github.com/ZenHive/harness) builds `param_keys: Map.keys(params)` and calls `apply/3` in that order. For a 2-arg tool `roadmap__list(project_name, status)`, `Map.keys` yields `[:status, :project_name]`, so a chat call `{project_name: "rexex", status: "pending"}` dispatches as `Roadmap.list("pending", "rexex")` → `{:error, {:unknown_project, "pending"}}`. Single-param tools and tools whose hash order happens to match are unaffected, which is why it surfaced only on the first 2-required-param tool.

descripex already has the ordered data at compile time (`params:` is an ordered keyword list; `Keyword.keys(declared_params)` and `extract_clause_param_names/1` both compute it during `__api__` generation). The fix is to persist it instead of dropping it in `build_params_map/1`'s `Map.new/2`.

Add an ordered param-name list to the `__api__(name)` result — e.g. `param_order: [:project_name, :status]` (positional param names in declaration order, including defaulted ones). Keep `hints[:params]` as-is for backward compatibility; `param_order` is the new authoritative ordering surface. Document that MCP-dispatch consumers must use `param_order` (not `Map.keys(params)`) to build positional argument lists.

Cross-ref / first consumer: once shipped, harness's `Harness.Chat.Tools.build_apply_args/2` switches from `Map.keys(params)` to `module.__api__(fun).param_order`. Coordinate the harness bump in github.com/ZenHive/harness — the harness side is currently held (no interim workaround) pending this fix.
task.implemented: Added param_order to __api__/0 and __api__/1 entries via build_param_order/1 in __before_compile__ (positional param names in declaration order, incl. defaults). hints[:params] map unchanged. Documented in moduledoc that MCP-dispatch consumers must order args by param_order. Added param_order test block with non-alphabetical apply/3 round-trip.

task.title: Emit typed JSON Schema for kind:value params — typeless properties make MCP clients mis-serialize
acceptance_criteria: build_property/1 (lib/descripex/mcp.ex:121) no longer emits a description-only (typeless) JSON Schema property for a kind:value param that lacks a typespec-derived `schema`. Every emitted property carries a JSON Schema `type` (or a oneOf/enum) so an MCP client can serialize the value without guessing.

Scalars get the right primitive type; atom-valued params emit `type: "string"` (with an enum/description hint where the accepted atoms are known) so a client sends a plain string the consumer can coerce, not a guessed shape; keyword/list/struct params emit a declared object/array type rather than no type.

A param with an Elixir `\\ default` is reflected so consumers can distinguish optional-with-runtime-default from required (today the static `default: nil` leaks into the schema and is indistinguishable from 'genuinely nil') — at minimum, optional params are not marked required, and the schema does not assert a misleading default.
Existing typespec-derived schemas (JSONSpec.convert path, mcp.ex:123-125) are unchanged — this only fills the typeless fallback branch.

Tests: Descripex.MCP.tools/1 over a fixture module with kind:value scalar, atom, and keyword-list params asserts each property has a concrete `type`; a regression test pins that no emitted property is description-only.

Coordinated with the consumer-side fix in harness Task 259 (harness Chat.Tools boundary). This task fixes the SCHEMA EMISSION (so clients serialize right); harness 259 fixes the dispatch-boundary coercion/decoding. Land both so the MCP param boundary stops returning empty/wrong for ordinary calls.
out_of_scope: The harness-side dispatch boundary (resolve_param/build_apply_args/decode_param) — that is harness Task 259.
Changing the api() macro's param-declaration syntax — only the JSON Schema emitted FROM existing declarations.
task.body:
CROSS-REPO with harness Task 259 ("Fix the MCP param boundary once and for all"). Filed 2026-06-12 from a harness session where every result_store aggregate MCP tool returned empty. Root cause spans both repos and descripex owns the upstream half.

THE DESCRIPEX GAP. Descripex.MCP.build_property/1 (lib/descripex/mcp.ex:118-126) converts a param hint to a JSON Schema property: if `details[:schema]` is present (a typespec ran through JSONSpec.convert) it merges description into it; OTHERWISE it returns a DESCRIPTION-ONLY property with no `"type"`. So any `kind: :value` param without a typespec-derived schema is advertised to MCP clients as a typeless property. With no type, an MCP/LLM client has nothing to serialize against — it stringifies structured args, sends plain strings for atoms, omits optionals, or guesses — and the consumer's typed guards then reject or mis-handle them.

DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOMS OBSERVED IN HARNESS (the consumer):
  - Optional param omitted -> consumer substitutes the static `default: nil` from the schema, overriding the Elixir `\\ configured()` runtime default -> aggregate_* tools hit a disabled guard and return empty {} / run_count 0, while the underlying data is healthy (186 records, in-process aggregates return real numbers).
  - Atom param (`:codex`,`:ecto`) -> client sends "codex"; consumer's is_atom/1 guard rejects it.
  - {module,opts} / struct param -> inexpressible as JSON at all; the tool advertises an uncallable shape.
  Harness already shipped two consumer-side band-aids for the same boundary (a702a54 JSON-string decode; task 248 legacy-empty field) — the durable fix is to stop emitting typeless schemas HERE so clients serialize correctly in the first place.

THE FIX (this task): make build_property/1 always emit a concrete `type`. For kind:value without a typespec, infer/declare the JSON type — scalar primitives, `type:"string"`(+enum hint) for atoms, object/array for keyword/struct params — and reflect optional-vs-required honestly so a static `default: nil` no longer masquerades as the real runtime default. descripex is the source of truth for the MCP tool contract; a typeless property is a contract gap, and the primary consumer (harness) drives an AI orchestrator over exactly this surface.

Pairs with harness Task 259 (consumer-side coercion + a Manifest-wide sweep test). Land them together; neither alone closes the class.
task.implemented: enrich_with_specs/2 fills hints.params.<name>.schema from the function's @spec for kind:value params lacking an explicit schema:; JSONSpec.convert over spec_to_quoted arg ASTs, with normalize_remote_aliases for String.t() and safe_convert skipping unconvertible/term types. build_property now emits concrete type/enum. Tests in mcp_test.exs cover scalar/atom/enum/list + a typeless-regression pin.

task.title: Reconcile __api__/0 spec-enrichment with the BEAM doc-chunk hints (or document the asymmetry)
acceptance_criteria: The relationship between __api__/0 hints and Code.fetch_docs meta[:hints] under spec-enrichment is either reconciled (Option A) or explicitly documented as intentional (Option B) in moduledoc + CONSUMING.md
If documented as intentional, descripex ships (or documents) the canonical way for a consumer to compare the two surfaces without false positives on injected schema keys
A test pins the chosen contract
CHANGELOG notes the consumer-facing guidance
out_of_scope: The safe_convert rescue-broadening fix shipped in 0.9.1 (separate, already done)
task.body:
Since v0.8/0.9 (Tasks 22/23), `enrich_with_specs/2` fills `hints.params.<name>.schema` (and opts schema) from `@spec` at **runtime** inside `__api__/0`, but the BEAM doc chunk written at compile time (`Code.fetch_docs/1` → `meta[:hints]`) is NOT enriched (a module can't read its own specs at `__before_compile__`). So for any param that gains a spec-derived schema, `module.__api__()` hints and `Code.fetch_docs` `meta[:hints]` now DIVERGE.

This breaks consumers that assert the two are equal. Concrete first reporter: Cartouche's `descripex_validation_test.exs` ("every @doc hints: block is attached to the correctly-named function") cross-checks `meta.hints in __api__/0 hints` to detect `api()` misattachment; under descripex 0.9 it fails purely on the injected `schema` key, a false positive. Cartouche worked around it by comparing modulo `:schema` (commit references this task).

Decide the contract and either fix or document:
- Option A: make `__api__/0` and the doc-chunk hints consistent for equality-based consumers — e.g. expose an un-enriched view, or a documented `drop_runtime_schema/1` normalizer descripex ships so consumers don't hand-roll one.
- Option B: declare the asymmetry intentional and document it prominently (moduledoc + CONSUMING.md + CHANGELOG): `__api__/0` is the runtime-enriched introspection surface; the doc chunk is the raw declared surface; consumers must not assert equality across the two.

Either way, ship a test that pins the chosen contract so it doesn't silently drift again.
task.implemented: normalize_for_doc_compare/1 + documented asymmetry (Option B); moduledoc + CONSUMING.md + CHANGELOG + 3 tests

task.title: Fix pre-existing Dialyzer pattern_match warning in lib/descripex.ex (macro-generated 'false can never match true')
task.body:
`mix dialyzer.json` reports one `pattern_match` warning: `The pattern 'false' can never match the type 'true'`, attributed to `lib/descripex.ex:1` (line 1 = Dialyzer can't pinpoint, so it is macro-generated code — likely the `api`/`__before_compile__`/`__api__` expansion).

Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: present at tag v0.9.1 (verified via worktree), so it has shipped in 0.7.0-0.10.0. Not a publish blocker, but it is the only outstanding Dialyzer warning and breaks the "0 warnings" gate.

Investigation path: find which generated clause produces a false/true guard pattern that is statically decidable. Expand the macro for a fixture module (Macro.expand / :debug_info) to locate the dead clause, then remove the impossible branch or restructure so Dialyzer sees a reachable pattern.
task.implemented: No code change needed -- verified already fixed at HEAD. mix dialyzer.json reports 0 warnings on 2026-08-22, confirmed by stashing the working-tree lib/descripex.ex and re-running against the committed version: still 0. The macro-generated 'false can never match true' pattern_match warning was removed by the earlier refactor that dropped the provably-always-true is_map/1 guard from safe_convert/1 (its replacement comment documents exactly that reasoning); the task was simply never closed. Kept as a done record rather than superseded, because the warning it describes was real and is now gone.

task.title: Add public `emit_api/3` macro for compile-time / for-comprehension api declarations
acceptance_criteria: `emit_api/3` is a documented public macro; `import Descripex` in `__using__/1` exposes it (emit_api: 3).

A test module declares an api via `emit_api/3` from inside a for-comprehension with variable opts; `__api__/0` returns the correct entry (name, param_order, hints) — proving the path `api/3` can't serve.
`@doc` text + `@doc hints:` are emitted identically to the equivalent `api/3` call for literal opts (no schema: keys).
Compile-time validation still fires for emit_api declarations: a wrong param name (or missing def) declared via `emit_api/3` raises `CompileError` at __before_compile__, same as `api/3`.

Schema-footgun guard: `emit_api/3` raises `ArgumentError` at expansion if `opts` is a literal keyword-list AST (message points the caller to `api/3`, which would have run preprocess_schemas). This removes the common misuse where a literal `schema: float()` would land raw in hints. Variable-opts callers (the for-comprehension case) pass through; the @doc states they must pre-convert any `schema:` keys.
CHANGELOG entry; minor version bump (emit_api/3 is additive).
out_of_scope: Making `api/3` itself tolerate variable opts (would require deferring preprocess_schemas to before_compile — separate, larger change).
Schema preprocessing inside emit_api (explicitly skipped; caller pre-converts).
task.body:
`api/3` runs `preprocess_schemas(opts)` at macro-expansion time, which calls
`Keyword.get/2` on the opts AST — so it ONLY works when `opts` is a literal
keyword-list AST. Callers that build opts inside a `for`-comprehension or any
macro-time variable (opts is then a `{:var, _, _}` AST node, not a list) cannot
use `api/3` — `preprocess_schemas` raises.

Real consumer gap: ccxt_client generates ~241 unified API declarations by
looping over `Unified.method_defs/0` and building per-method `api_opts` as a
compile-time variable. It cannot call `api/3`. ccxt_client carries a *vendored
fork* of descripex SOLELY to add this macro (`vendor/descripex`,
`override: true`) — it can't switch to the hex package until this ships.

Add `emit_api/3` as a PUBLIC macro: same emissions as `api/3` but skips
`preprocess_schemas/1` (caller pre-converts any `schema:` keys; for-comprehension
callers don't use them). Reference impl already proven in the vendor fork:

    defmacro emit_api(name, description, opts) do
      quote do
        @descripex_api_declarations {unquote(name), unquote(description), unquote(opts)}
        @doc Descripex.generate_doc(unquote(description), unquote(opts))
        @doc hints: Descripex.build_hints(unquote(description), unquote(opts))
      end
    end

Also add `emit_api: 3` to the `import Descripex` list in `__using__/1`.
`generate_doc/2` and `build_hints/2` are already public — no other surface change.

Retires the vendor fork: once released, ccxt_client's mix.exs swaps
`{:descripex, path: "vendor/descripex", override: true}` for the hex requirement
and replaces the fully-qualified `Descripex.emit_api/3` call with the imported form.
task.implemented: emit_api/3 public macro in lib/descripex.ex: same @doc/@doc hints:/@descripex_api_declarations emissions as api/3 but skips preprocess_schemas, so it accepts variable (for-comprehension) opts. Imported via __using__ (emit_api: 3). Guard raises ArgumentError on a literal keyword-list opts (steers to api/3, the schema-footgun mitigation). __before_compile__ validation still fires (shared accumulator). 5 tests in descripex_test.exs: for-comprehension round-trip, api/3-can't-serve (FunctionClauseError), emit==api identical doc+hints for literal opts, validation-fires (CompileError on wrong param name), literal-opts-rejected (ArgumentError). CHANGELOG + minor bump 0.10.0 -> 0.11.0. CLAUDE.md macro section documents it.

task.title: Fold nonempty_list/[T,...]/union spec types so MCP params stop shipping silently typeless
acceptance_criteria: A kind:value param whose @spec type is nonempty_list(T) or [T, ...] emits the same JSON Schema as [T] -- verified for T = String.t(), atom(), and a union

REGRESSION GUARD, verify FIRST: the two union forms json_spec already converts keep their exact current output -- :buy | :sell -> %{"enum" => ["buy", "sell"], "type" => "string"} and String.t() | nil -> %{"type" => "string"}. Both have members that raise standalone (:buy, nil), so any per-member fold must run only AFTER a whole-union convert attempt, never instead of it. schema: :buy | :sell is a documented descripex feature (SchemaFixture) and String.t() | nil appears in the motivating @spec.

A union json_spec rejects wholesale is then folded per member: if every non-nil member yields the same schema, emit it (atom() | String.t() -> {"type": "string"}); if they differ, emit anyOf (integer() | String.t()) rather than picking one member
These forms work both as a list element type and as a top-level param type
Descripex.MCP.tools/1 over a fixture with such a @spec emits a property carrying a concrete type -- a regression test pins that no property is description-only
safe_convert/1 distinguishes 'inexpressible, correctly skipped' from 'expressible but the converter raised'; the second is observable (a compile-time warning or a queryable count) rather than silent
Genuinely inexpressible types (term()/any(), tuples, non-String remote types, bitstrings) still skip without a guessed shape, and an explicit schema: still wins
out_of_scope: A PR to dannote/json_spec for the underlying forms -- the clean complement, not a prerequisite; this fix is a local AST pre-pass
Changing the MCP wire schema shape (inputSchema stays a JSON object per spec)
The __api__/0 vs BEAM doc-chunk enrichment asymmetry (Task 24, already resolved as documented-intentional)
task.body:
Spec-derived param schemas ship silently typeless for several type forms json_spec cannot convert, so an api()-exposed function is advertised over MCP but is uncallable with its documented argument: the client sends a JSON array, the callee receives its string form.

VERIFIED 2026-08-22 against json_spec ~> 1.1 in this checkout, by probing JSONSpec.convert/1 directly (ASTs pre-normalized through normalize_remote_aliases/1) and by compiling a fixture module to disk and reading Descripex.MCP.tools/1:

  [String.t()]                       -> %{"type" => "array", "items" => %{"type" => "string"}}
  list(String.t())                   -> same
  nonempty_list(String.t())          -> ArgumentError
  nonempty_list(atom())              -> ArgumentError
  nonempty_list(atom() | String.t()) -> ArgumentError
  [atom() | String.t()]              -> ArgumentError (unsupported union)
  [String.t(), ...]                  -> ArgumentError
  atom() | String.t()                -> ArgumentError (unsupported union)

End-to-end proof: a fixture with @spec register([String.t()], nonempty_list(atom() | String.t())) :: :ok emits
  warm_paths -> %{"type" => "array", "items" => %{"type" => "string"}, "description" => ...}
  languages  -> %{"description" => "languages"}          # no type
Real-world hit: Harness.Dispatch.register_project/8. Calling the tool with languages: ["elixir"] delivered the literal string ["elixir"] to the callee, which rejected it; registration only succeeded via a hand-rolled JSON-RPC tools/call carrying a real array.

TWO LAYERS. (1) json_spec supports only the [T] and list(T) forms. nonempty_list(T) fails for EVERY T -- this is not union-specific. Non-enum, non-nullable unions fail ANYWHERE, not only as a list element type. (2) descripex's safe_convert/1 (lib/descripex.ex, the rescue over ArgumentError / CaseClauseError / FunctionClauseError) turns that into :skip, so the param ships typeless with no warning and no manifest-level signal. :skip is the right call for genuinely inexpressible types -- the cases its rescue comment enumerates -- but here it hides a type that IS expressible.

THE FIX belongs here, not upstream, and it splits across TWO sites -- do not try to do all of it in the AST pre-pass.

(a) AST pre-pass (normalize_remote_aliases/1, or a sibling walker it composes with). This is a Macro.prewalk returning an AST, so only rewrites with a type-AST form belong here: fold nonempty_list(T) -> [T] and the [T, ...] literal -> [T]. Both are pure AST-to-AST. Nothing about unions fits here -- deciding a union requires CONVERTING each member and comparing the resulting JSON Schema maps, and anyOf has no type-AST spelling at all.

(b) Converter step (safe_convert/1, or a new function it delegates to). Union handling lives here, AFTER the whole-union JSONSpec.convert/1 attempt has been made and raised. Order is load-bearing: json_spec already converts the all-atom enum form (:buy | :sell -> enum) and the nullable form (String.t() | nil -> {"type" => "string"}), and in BOTH cases individual members raise standalone (:buy and nil are not convertible types). A per-member fold applied first therefore REGRESSES two forms that work today -- :buy | :sell would go typeless, which is the exact bug this task fixes, and schema: :buy | :sell is a documented feature. So: try the union whole; on ArgumentError, drop nil members (json_spec itself discards nullability -- String.t() | nil yields a bare string schema), convert each remaining member, and if they all agree emit that single schema, else emit %{"anyOf" => [...]}.

On unions, do NOT "reduce to the widest expressible member" -- that is lossy and has no meaning for integer() | String.t(). Use the measured fact instead: atom() and String.t() BOTH convert to %{"type" => "string"}, so folding atom() | String.t() is lossless because the members agree, not because one is wider. No guessing step.

Independently -- and this is what let the gap ship unnoticed -- distinguish "inexpressible, correctly skipped" from "expressible but the converter choked". The second deserves a compile-time warning or a queryable count, so a typeless param on an api() surface is visible before an MCP client trips over it.

Origin: zen_websocket -> harness -> here, discovered 2026-08-20 registering a project through harness's dispatch-register_project MCP tool. BUGS.md #1 carries the discovery narrative and the raw probe table; THIS task body is authoritative on the fix -- where BUGS.md's "suggested direction" paragraph differs, follow the task.
task.implemented: Two-stage conversion in lib/descripex.ex. Stage 1, normalize_type_ast/1 (AST->AST prewalk): folds nonempty_list(T) and the [T, ...] literal to [T], and rewrites module()/node() to atom() (the exact type Elixir defines them as; json_spec knows neither name). Stage 2, convert_type/1: tries JSONSpec.convert on the WHOLE type first -- load-bearing, since the members of the two union forms json_spec does accept raise standalone (:buy and nil), so a member-first fold would have regressed :buy | :sell and String.t() | nil to typeless -- and only decomposes on rejection: a union drops nil members, converts the rest, collapses to the shared schema when they agree (atom() | String.t() -> {"type": "string"}) or emits anyOf when they differ (integer() | String.t()); a [T]/list(T) whose element was rejected is rebuilt around the folded element schema. Visibility: new public Descripex.typeless_params/1 lists every kind:value param still shipping without a schema, tagged :no_spec / :no_type_info / :unconvertible -- only the last is actionable, so a CI gate filters on it. It immediately caught four typeless params in descripex's OWN surface (Manifest.build/1 and Describe.describe/3 take [module()]); the module() fold closed all but MCP.tools/2's keyword(), which stays honestly skipped. Also fixed a real defect found by the tests: module_typeless_params/1 needed Code.ensure_loaded?/1 before function_exported?/3, which answers false for an unloaded module -- the same false negative was in CONSUMING.md's detection advice and is corrected there too. New Descripex.Test.SpecUnionFixture (register/6, store/3, load/3, untyped/1) plus 14 tests across mcp_test.exs and descripex_test.exs, including regression guards pinning the enum and nullable union output. CHANGELOG + CLAUDE.md + CONSUMING.md updated; minor bump 0.12.1 -> 0.13.0 (typeless_params/1 is additive).

task.title: short_name returns a string, not an atom — drop String.to_atom on caller-supplied module lists
task.body: Retroactive record of the v0.12.0 breaking change, filed 2026-08-22 so the shipped surface is traceable from the roadmap and not only from CHANGELOG. Describe.describe/1 and Discoverable's generated describe/0 return short_name: "funding" where they previously returned :funding. Arguments are unaffected — describe("funding"), describe(:funding) and describe(MyLib.Funding) all still resolve; only code that pattern-matches the RETURNED short_name needs updating. Removing the atom creation (rather than suppressing the check) closed the last reach.check --smells finding, unsafe_atom_creation: a short name is a label derived from a module list the CALLER supplies, so interning it grows the atom table on input this library does not control.
task.implemented: Describe.short_name/1 returns a binary; the unknown-short-name error lists available names as strings without atomizing the module list. Full rationale, including why String.to_existing_atom/1 and compile-time interning were both unsound, in CHANGELOG 0.12.0.

task.title: mix ci advisory-database guard broke under Elixir 1.18's mix cmd argument re-parsing
task.body: Retroactive record of the v0.12.1 fix, filed 2026-08-22 for roadmap traceability. The advisory-database-present guard in mix ci was an inline sh -c 'if …; then …; fi' passed through mix cmd. Elixir 1.18 joins mix cmd's arguments into one string and re-parses it through the shell, so the guard became a syntax error on CI while working locally under 1.19+, which passes argv straight to System.cmd/3. The guard is load-bearing: mix_audit clones its advisory database at runtime and discards the clone's exit status, so a failed clone audits zero advisories and still exits 0 — a green CI that checked nothing.
task.implemented: Guard extracted to bin/advisory-db-present.sh, which behaves identically under both argument-passing regimes. Shipped alongside the ex_ast 0.13.1 / sobelow 0.15.0 / tidewave 0.8.4 tooling bumps.

task.title: Declare 1.0.0 — SemVer contract and named public API surface
acceptance_criteria: mix.exs @version is 1.0.0 and README's installation snippet pins `~> 1.0`
README carries an API Stability section naming the covered surface and explicitly excluding generate_doc/2, build_hints/2, enrich_with_specs/2 with the reason (macro-emitted call targets)
CHANGELOG 1.0.0 entry states no behavioural change over 0.13.0 and repeats the exclusion
mix precommit.full is green
~/.claude/includes/elixir-setup.md dep pin updated to ~> 1.0 per the repo's Release Checklist
out_of_scope: Any behavioural or API change — a 1.0 that also changes behaviour cannot be verified as a pure stability declaration
task.body:
Cut 1.0.0 as a stability declaration, not a feature release: no behavioural change over 0.13.0.

WHY NOW. Every roadmap task is done, superseded, or explicitly rejected by design (Task 15 — schema validation, deferred on the JSON-Schema-validates-JSON impedance mismatch; Tasks 29-32 — theoria binding, hard-blocked on an unpublished upstream). The declaration surface (api/2, api/3, emit_api/3 and its option set) has not broken since 0.6.0. Consumers pin `~> 0.x`, which under SemVer accepts a possible break on every minor; the whole point of the bump is to give them `~> 1.0` and have it mean something.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING, and it is the only real content of this task: which functions the promise covers. Three public functions are public ONLY because macro expansion emits calls to them from the consuming module — Descripex.generate_doc/2 and build_hints/2 (compile time, from the api() expansion) and enrich_with_specs/2 (runtime, from the generated __api__/0). They are the call target of generated code, not an API to invoke directly. Freezing them under SemVer would constrain how api() emits for no consumer benefit, so they are named as excluded in README's API Stability section and in the CHANGELOG entry. Everything else is in: use Descripex, the three declaration macros and their options, the generated __api__/0 and __api__/1 and the hints map shape, Manifest.build/1, Describe.describe/1..3, MCP.tools/1, use Descripex.Discoverable, typeless_params/1, normalize_for_doc_compare/1, and the mix descripex.manifest task with its JSON output shape.

One further carve-out, documented in the same place: schemas DERIVED from a @spec (as opposed to an explicit schema:) track what json_spec can express. A json_spec upgrade that turns a previously typeless property into a typed one is a widening, treated as minor, with typeless_params/1 as the way to see which params it affects.

Also fixes README's installation snippet, which pinned `~> 0.7` — six minor releases behind what was on Hex.
task.implemented: Version bumped 0.13.0 -> 1.0.0. README gained an API Stability section naming the SemVer-covered surface (use Descripex; api/2,3 + emit_api/3 and their option set; generated __api__/0,1 and the hints map shape; Manifest.build/1; Describe.describe/1..3; MCP.tools/1; use Descripex.Discoverable; typeless_params/1; normalize_for_doc_compare/1; mix descripex.manifest and its JSON shape) and explicitly excluding generate_doc/2, build_hints/2 and enrich_with_specs/2 as macro-emitted call targets rather than a callable API, plus the json_spec-derived-schema widening carve-out. CHANGELOG 1.0.0 entry records no behavioural change over 0.13.0. README install pin corrected ~> 0.7 -> ~> 1.0; ~/.claude/includes/elixir-setup.md pin ~> 0.13 -> ~> 1.0 and marketplace skills re-synced.
